sections.title: Summary
sections.text: The applicant is a maize and inputs trader in Eastern Province seeking K25,000 for 12 months to buy seed and fertiliser. The business has traded for 7 years. The risk band is Low, with an estimated probability of default of 1.2%.

sections.title: Business and cash flow
sections.text: The business shows 12 months of statement history. Average monthly income is K19,896, while the applicant declared K20,000. Income peaks in May 2026 at K47,760, which is 2.8 times a typical month. This pattern matches the expected season, with a season fit of 0.98. After adjusting for the season, income variation is 12%. The weakest month, adjusted for the season, is January 2026 at 80% of a typical month. Harvest-season income is 109% of the seasonal prediction.

sections.title: Risks and mitigants
sections.text: The main risk factor is the lack of credit-bureau history, creating a thin file. Mitigants include the strong surplus cover for the new instalment, zero days in overdraft, and low income variation beyond the normal season. The largest customer accounts for 11% of payments, and 57% of income is received via mobile money.

facts_given_to_model:
Business type: Maize and inputs trader in Eastern Province (agriculture). Loan purpose: Seed and fertiliser stock ahead of the planting season.
Checks (mocked services in this prototype): PACRA confirms the business is registered and active; ZRA confirms the TPIN and tax compliance; the credit bureau has no history for the applicant (thin file).
Risk band: Low.

Figures (placeholder: meaning = value):
{{months}}: Months of statement history = 12
{{mean_monthly_income}}: Average monthly business income = K19,896
{{monthly_income}}: Business income by month = K238,755
{{raw_income_cv}}: Month-to-month income variation = 53%
{{deseasoned_income_cv}}: Income variation after allowing for the season = 12%
{{peak_month}}: The month with the most income = May 2026
{{peak_month_income}}: Income in the peak month = K47,760
{{peak_to_median}}: Peak month compared with a typical month = 2.8x
{{overdraft_day_share}}: Share of days the Absa account was overdrawn = 0%
{{top_customer_share}}: Share of customer payments from the largest customer = 11%
{{mobile_money_share}}: Share of income received by mobile money = 57%
{{mean_monthly_committed}}: Average monthly supplier, rent, wages and loan payments = K11,340
{{mean_monthly_surplus}}: Average monthly surplus after committed costs = K8,557
{{new_instalment}}: Monthly instalment on the requested loan = K2,667
{{debt_service_coverage}}: Surplus cover for the new instalment = 3.2x
{{unverified_income_share}}: Share of income on unverified rows = 0%
{{season_peak_ratio}}: Peak the business's season predicts, against a typical month = 2.5x
{{season_fit}}: How closely income follows the expected season = 0.98
{{weakest_month}}: The weakest month, allowing for the season = January 2026
{{weakest_month_ratio}}: Weakest month against a typical month, allowing for the season = 80%
{{harvest_ratio}}: Harvest-season income against what the season predicts = 109%
{{requested_amount}}: Loan requested = K25,000
{{tenor_months}}: Loan term in months = 12
{{years_trading}}: Years in business = 7
{{declared_monthly_turnover}}: Monthly turnover the applicant declared = K20,000
{{pd}}: Estimated probability of default = 1.2%

Findings:
- Income follows the business's expected season (a predictable peak, not a risk) (context); evidence: {{peak_month_income}}, {{peak_to_median}}, {{season_fit}}, {{deseasoned_income_cv}}

What raises the risk score: no credit-bureau history (thin file)
What lowers it: surplus cover for the new instalment; days spent in overdraft; how much income varies beyond the normal season

Verification: all statements reconcile and transfers match Absa's records
Rows needing review: 0, of which 0 contain text that reads like instructions (treated as data).
